articles.title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’

events.summary: India's government will reduce the prices of 137 cancer drugs starting next month following a Supreme Court ruling deeming mark-ups 'extortion'. The ruling originated from a 2022 case filed by a patient who could not afford treatment.
events.why: Mandated price cuts on critical oncology drugs directly alleviate life-threatening financial hardship for millions facing severe disease across India.

articles.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
Ebola: Kenya announces second death

events.summary: A 65-year-old woman became the second person to die of Ebola in Kenya. She was a close relative of the first victim, who had recently travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
events.why: Cross-border transmission and secondary local deaths from Ebola pose severe epidemic risks requiring immediate containment.

articles.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
Jordan: Karak church shooting leaves 7 dead, dozens injured

events.summary: Gunmen killed seven people and wounded 34 others during an attack at a church funeral in Jordan's southern Karak governorate. Authorities have initiated a manhunt for the perpetrators.
events.why: A mass-casualty armed assault at a place of worship signals serious domestic security threats and risks communal destabilization in Jordan.

articles.title: Israeli PM pledges massive military operation after West Bank checkpoint attack

events.summary: Israel's Prime Minister announced plans for a major military operation in the West Bank. The move follows a checkpoint attack by two Palestinian gunmen that resulted in the deaths of two Israeli soldiers.
events.why: The launch of a major military offensive carries severe casualties, territorial escalation, and wide regional repercussions.

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire

events.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a US-brokered localized ceasefire in the frontline city of Oleshky to address a humanitarian crisis. President Zelenskyy noted that negotiators will convene for broader talks next month.
events.why: This represents a critical humanitarian pause and a potential diplomatic opening for wider negotiations in the ongoing conflict.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula, Bolsonaro draw thousands to election-eve rallies
Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro about even ahead of election run-off: Poll

events.summary: Thousands of supporters attended final election rallies for Brazilian presidential candidates Lula and Bolsonaro ahead of a close run-off vote. The result will determine whether Brazil maintains a left-wing government or turns to the right.
events.why: A decisive election in Latin America's largest economy carries major national governance and international policy consequences.

articles.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions

events.summary: Ukraine's military announced that Starlink satellite connections have stabilized after experiencing network restrictions. The previous slowdowns had hindered military and drone operations for a week.
events.why: The reliability of commercial satellite communications directly determines operational capability and battlefield effectiveness in the Ukraine war.

articles.title: Ukraine: Starlink satellite speeds restored to normal
Ukraine says Starlink is back to normal after disruptions

events.summary: Ukraine stated that Starlink satellite speeds have returned to normal after prior network limits. The restrictions had disrupted Ukrainian military operations and strained relations with the United States.
events.why: Restoring high-speed satellite communications ends a disruption that degraded Ukrainian defense operations and heightened allied geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: Deadly shooting near Paris is a 'racist terrorist attack', Macron says

events.summary: One person was killed and five others were wounded in a series of attacks near Paris described by President Macron as a racist terrorist attack. A suspected gunman has been apprehended by authorities.
events.why: Deadly extremist violence represents a severe domestic security breach with potential sociopolitical repercussions.

articles.title: Trump administration sues to block certification of upcoming Alaska election

events.summary: The Justice Department has filed a lawsuit seeking to block certification of an upcoming election in Alaska. The suit argues that having two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the ballot could confuse voters.
events.why: Federal intervention in state election certification processes sets a notable legal precedent and directly challenges electoral administration.

articles.title: Trump lauds Melania over Russia-Ukraine localised ceasefire deal

events.summary: Donald Trump credited the First Lady following the establishment of a localized Russia-Ukraine ceasefire in Oleshky. The pause halts fighting in the frontline city.
events.why: Any cessation of hostilities, even localized, alters military dynamics on the ground in an active war zone.

articles.title: Magnitude-7 earthquake hits Tibet, killing at least 16 and destroying hundreds of homes

events.summary: A magnitude-7 earthquake struck the northern regional city of Nagqu in Tibet, killing at least 16 people and injuring 54. Hundreds of homes were destroyed, and at least seven aftershocks were recorded as search and rescue operations began.
events.why: A major earthquake causes immediate loss of life, widespread displacement, and severe infrastructure destruction requiring regional emergency response.

articles.title: Helen Haines’s condition improves days after losing both legs from alleged attack

events.summary: Australian independent MP Helen Haines is in serious but stable condition after losing both legs in an alleged attack. Her medical status was confirmed by Melbourne's Alfred Hospital.
events.why: A violent, disabling attack on a sitting member of parliament raises urgent national security and political stability concerns.

articles.title: Additional 178 cases of measles reported by US health authorities amid outbreak

events.summary: US health authorities reported 178 new measles cases this week across at least 43 outbreaks. Total nationwide cases reached 4,588, which is more than double the count recorded in 2025.
events.why: A rapid escalation in outbreaks of a highly contagious, preventable disease threatens public health systems and vulnerable populations nationwide.

articles.title: ICC prosecutor says court making ‘significant progress’ despite US sanctions

events.summary: The deputy prosecutor of the International Criminal Court stated that court staff are experiencing banking issues due to new US sanctions, but operations remain unhindered. The court continues to make significant progress despite the diplomatic measures.
events.why: Unilateral economic sanctions targeting an international judicial body test the resilience and global authority of international law.

articles.title: Could Israel’s military crackdown influence Tuesday’s election?

events.summary: Israel is preparing a complete lockdown of the occupied West Bank following a gunfight in Hebron. The measures come shortly before a national election.
events.why: A full regional lockdown restricts civilian movement for hundreds of thousands and escalates security friction.

articles.title: Healey’s first budget to include big devolution package to boost growth

events.summary: The UK Chancellor's upcoming budget will include a significant devolution package intended to increase regional spending powers and foster growth in England. Local leaders, supported by Andy Burnham, will see reduced reliance on Westminster for funding.
events.why: Structural devolution alters public spending control and governance across English regions, directly shaping local economic development.

articles.title: More than one million Lula supporters rally on eve of Brazilian election runoff

events.summary: More than one million supporters of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva rallied on Rio de Janeiro's beach ahead of the presidential election runoff. Nearly 159 million voters are eligible to participate in the contest between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.
events.why: The outcome of Brazil's presidential election directly impacts the governance and policy trajectory of Latin America's largest nation and its millions of citizens.

articles.title: Serbian elections: A country where students may actually take power
Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament

events.summary: Serbia is holding early parliamentary elections amid significant tension and competitive challenges from student movements against the country's most powerful politicians.
events.why: Early national elections can shift Serbia's domestic power balance and influence regional stability in the Western Balkans.

articles.title: Fire engulfs Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat catches fire, police say
Suspect arrested over fire at Hitler’s ‘Eagle’s Nest’ retreat in Bavaria

events.summary: A fire engulfed the historic Eagle's Nest retreat in Bavaria. Bavarian police have detained a 33-year-old German man in connection with the incident.
events.why: The arson of a prominent historical site raises criminal and cultural heritage concerns.
